Advances: specled.package

Orchestrated under epic specled_-233 (2026-07-26), shipping on one PR with specled_-48i, specled_-gai, specled_-ymn.

SEQUENCING: blocked by sibling specled_-48i because both edit .spec/specs/package.spec.md. You will be spawned only after 48i merges into the epic branch, so your base SHA already contains its changes. Do not re-do 48i's concepts_guide content-lint work.

## Context

Advisory findings from the specled_-6fn test-critic pass and the specled_-6fn ship-it critical review (2026-07-23), deferred out of those tickets as future hardening of test/docs_identifier_lint_test.exs. Go-live triage (2026-07-25) split the two LIVE spec inaccuracies out to P1 gate ticket specled_-cz0; this ticket holds only the deferred hardening items.

## Pre-flight corrections (orchestrator, 2026-07-26) — parts of this ticket are ALREADY DONE

This ticket accumulated four comments across three days. Current state of test/docs_identifier_lint_test.exs at base 402f4a27:

- `@token_patterns` (line 149) holds exactly FIVE families: `append_only/*`, `overlap/*`, `evidence/*`, `cross_field/*`, `branch_guard_*`. specled_-cz0 already did the widening described in the 2026-07-26 03:17 comment. A test at line 275 pins `length(@token_patterns) == 5` against the must's claim, and one at 291 asserts evidence/* and cross_field/* are guarded in both directions.
- The COVERAGE GAP item from the 2026-07-24 comment is therefore substantially CLOSED. `surface_target_*` and `scenario_cover_*` remain deliberately unguarded, and the must statement in package.spec.md already discloses them by name along with the four unusable stems (`detector_`, `decision_`, `verification_`, `requirement_`).
- The PRE-EXISTING SPEC INACCURACY item (triangulation.spec.md fabricated scenario) is DONE — shipped in specled_-cz0.

## Remaining scope — five items

1. A3 LOOKBEHIND BOUNDS. All five patterns lead with `(?<![\w/])` (comment at line 145, patterns 150-160). Its bounds are unbounded and untested: any token preceded by `/` is skipped, so e.g. `foo/append_only/deep_fabricated` is not flagged. Add boundary tests pinning BOTH directions, so tightening or loosening the lookbehind cannot silently change coverage: (a) a closure-file path segment such as `.../config/branch_guard_test.exs` stays suppressed, AND (b) a real backtick-delimited code on that same kind of line is still caught.

2. A4 SEVERITY-CORPUS ASYMMETRY. `severity_corpus/0` (line 189) is `normalize(guidance_files())` and deliberately excludes `.spec/**`, because spec scenarios quote atom-form config as the input under test. Real atom-form severities exist at .spec/specs/prose_guard.spec.md, branch_guard.spec.md and spec_drift_trailer.spec.md, so the exclusion is load-bearing but unasserted. Assert both arms: an atom-form severity in a guidance doc trips the line-227 test, the same form under `.spec/**` does not. Collapsing `severity_corpus` into `finding_code_corpus` (line 183) must break a test.

3. A5 DIGIT-BEARING CODES. The token char-class `[a-z_]` cannot represent a finding code containing a digit. Not a live defect — no emitted code has one — but the hand-maintained `@known_codes` mirror and the extraction pattern would silently diverge if one were added. Decide: widen the class, or assert that no emitted code contains a digit. PREFER THE ASSERTION — it is the cheaper guard and fails loudly the day someone adds one, whereas widening the class changes false-positive behavior for zero present benefit. Record the decision.

4. STALE-MARKER SWEEP. Nothing detects an allow-marker (`@allow_marker_pattern`, line 168) whose token has since become a real emitted code, or whose token no longer appears on its line. Either rots into a permanent unearned exemption. Add the detection.

5. TWO-WAY MIRROR. `@known_codes` (line 139) catches a code ADDED to lib/ but not one DELETED from it, so docs naming a now-dead code keep passing. Add the reverse direction. Note that specled.decision.doc_identifier_lint_spec_corpus rejects deriving the code set by reflection over lib/, so the mirror must stay hand-maintained; make it fail loudly in both directions rather than automating it away. SAME DEFECT SHAPE ONE LEVEL UP: that ADR declares `affects: specled.package`, but package.spec.md's `decisions:` list does not name it, so a reader who stops at the must has no in-corpus pointer to where the deliberate non-guarding of `surface_target_*` / `scenario_cover_*` is justified. Add it to the list.

## Allowed touches

- `test/docs_identifier_lint_test.exs` — the five hardening items.
- `.spec/specs/package.spec.md` — the `decisions:` list back-link, and the doc_identifier_integrity statement ONLY if a hardening item makes it factually inaccurate.
- `.spec/decisions/specled.decision.doc_identifier_lint_spec_corpus.md` — if the disclosure must record a decision you make (e.g. the A5 arm).
- `.spec/realization_hashes.json` — via its documented regeneration command, if the spec gate demands it.

Co-changing the `Advances:` subject spec above IS authorized: a green `mix spec.check --no-run-commands` outranks a narrow reading of Out of Scope. Do NOT weaken a requirement to make code pass.

## Out of Scope (files)

- `lib/**` — no production change is needed.
- `.spec/specs/triangulation.spec.md` — shipped in specled_-cz0.
- Any other subject's spec file.
- `CHANGELOG.md`, `VERSION`.

## Out of Scope (intent)

- Do NOT widen `@token_patterns` to `surface_target_*` / `scenario_cover_*`. Each needs its own hand-maintained allowlist, it is deferred under specled.decision.doc_identifier_lint_spec_corpus, and doing it would defeat this ticket's own point that "clean today" is not a coverage argument. If you conclude otherwise, say so in your completion record rather than doing it.
- Do not replace the hand-maintained mirror with reflection over lib/ — the ADR rejects that.
- No new dependencies in mix.exs.
- Do not relax an existing assertion to accommodate a new one.

## Verification (gates)

Final tier is change-scoped. Do NOT run the full suite — whole-system proof runs at the orchestrator merge gate and PR CI.

1. `mix compile --warnings-as-errors`
2. `mix test test/docs_identifier_lint_test.exs`
3. `mix spec.check --no-run-commands`
4. FALSIFIABILITY GATE — mandatory, and the whole point of this ticket. Every one of the five items must be a test that FAILS when the guard it pins is removed. This ticket exists because guards that cannot fail are worthless; adding assertions that pass in both directions would re-commit the same defect. For each item, demonstrate the failing direction locally (revert before commit) and record it, item by item, in your completion record.

Deferred widening identified while fixing specled_-cz0 (2026-07-25), belongs with the rest of the lint hardening here.

cz0 widened the doc-identifier lint from three guarded finding-code families to five, adding evidence/* (7 codes) and cross_field/* (8 codes). Those were the only remaining families carrying a namespace or ratified prefix — verified by extracting every code-shaped literal from lib/ (99 distinct) and grouping by prefix.

Two further clusters COULD be guarded and were deliberately left out of cz0:
  - surface_target_* (3 codes)
  - scenario_cover_* (2 codes)

Both currently collide with zero non-code identifiers in the scanned corpus, so a stem pattern would not false-positive today. That is the entire reason they are candidates — and also the reason to be careful, since "clean today" is exactly the property cz0 existed to stop relying on.

The larger bare-code stems are NOT candidates; measured against the corpus they each reject correct prose:
  detector_    → detector_unavailable_by_leg (review-output field) + a requirement id embedding the stem
  decision_    → 8 non-codes (decision_dir, decision_governance, decision_index, ...)
  verification_→ 4 non-codes
  requirement_ → 6 non-codes

Cost of the widening: two more hand-maintained allowlists. specled.decision.doc_identifier_lint_spec_corpus rejects deriving the code set by reflection over lib/, so there is no cheap way to keep them honest — which is why this pairs naturally with the two-way mirror and stale-marker items already scoped here.

Second item for this ticket's two-way-mirror scope, surfaced by cold verification of specled_-cz0 (2026-07-25).

The link between specled.package.doc_identifier_integrity and the ADR that governs its enforcement boundary is one-way:

  - .spec/decisions/specled.decision.doc_identifier_lint_spec_corpus.md declares `affects: specled.package`
  - .spec/specs/package.spec.md `decisions:` lists declarative_current_truth, local_skill_scaffold, explicit_subject_ownership, guided_reconciliation_loop — but NOT doc_identifier_lint_spec_corpus

Consequence, and why it is worth fixing rather than just noting: the must states which finding-code families are mechanically guarded, and the ADR is where the deliberate non-guarding of surface_target_* and scenario_cover_* is disclosed and justified. A reader who stops at the must has no in-corpus pointer to that disclosure. cz0 mitigated this by rewording the must so it cannot be read as claiming exhaustive coverage (commit b7b9eb1), but the mitigation is prose discipline, not a link — the next author to touch either file has nothing mechanical telling them the two are coupled.

This is the same defect shape already scoped here as the two-way mirror (@known_codes catches a code ADDED to lib/ but not one DELETED), one level up: subject → decision references are checked in one direction only, so a spec can silently lose its pointer to the ADR that qualifies it.
